radiology_report:
Erasmus MC
Department of Radiology
Date: 12 December 2024
Exam: mpMRI Prostate (3T)

Clinical indication: Elevated PSA 6.2 ng/mL, rising trend. Prior biopsy Gleason 3+4. Evaluate for focal lesion and local staging.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume: 23.05 mL.
T2-weighted imaging demonstrates a focal hypo-intense lesion in the peripheral zone of the left posterolateral base, measuring approximately 12 x 10 mm. On diffusion-weighted imaging, this region shows marked restricted diffusion with low ADC values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences demonstrate early and rapid wash-in of contrast within the same region. The transition zone appears unremarkable. No evidence of extracapsular extension, seminal vesicle invasion, or suspicious lymphadenopathy.

IMPRESSION:
Focal lesion in the left peripheral zone consistent with PI-RADS v2.1 category 4.
Prostate volume 23.05 mL; PSA density 0.269 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical T stage: cT1c.
csPCa predicted probability 0.8429154.

previous_notes.text: 05 Sep 2024 - Dr. P. van Dijk (GP): Patient presented for follow-up of rising PSA, now 4.3 ng/mL. A transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy was performed. The patient tolerated the procedure well and was discharged with standard antibiotic prophylaxis instructions. Awaiting pathology results.

previous_notes.author: Dr. P. van Dijk (GP)
previous_notes.text: 13 Jul 2023 - Dr. P. van Dijk (GP): Routine screening revealed an initial PSA of 1.4 ng/mL, which was within normal limits. The patient was advised to continue annual monitoring. No urinary symptoms or abnormalities on initial digital rectal examination were noted at that time.

pathology_report:
Biopsy 1 (05 September 2024): Prostate tissue fragments are submitted. Histological examination reveals a focus of acinar adenocarcinoma in the peripheral zone, left side. The tumour is assigned a Gleason score of 3+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 2. No cribriform or intraductal patterns are identified. Perineural invasion is not present.

Biopsy trajectory: The histological findings remain stable across the available biopsy timepoints, with persistent ISUP grade group 2 disease.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 2.
